[SWS_CM_00822] Minimum Send Interval monitoring for for method calls by the client
⌈
To protect receivers from flooding/overload, each method shall have a config-
urable Minimum Send Interval (see ServiceInterfaceDeploymentElement.min-
imumSendInterval), which specifies the minimum amount of time that shall pass
between two calls of the method by the client, i.e., the Minimum Send Interval limits the
maximum Tx frequency of a given method call in the network. If the application calls a
method by invoking theoperator() of the respective method class, ara::com shall
check, whether the time since the last successful handover of the method call the un-
derlying transmission layer is greater than the specified Minimum Send Interval, i.e.,
the Minimum Send Interval is not violated. If the operator() has never been invoked
before, this shall also successfully pass the Minimum Send Interval check. If the Mini-
mum Send Interval is not violated, ara::com shall process the method call by handing
it over to the transmission layer. The time of handover shall count as start of the new
Minimum Send Interval monitoring. If the Minimum Send Interval is violated, ara::com
shall discard the method call (see [SWS_CM_00196] and [SWS_CM_90435] ). If the
method was a Request&Response method, the error code ComErrc::kMinimum-
SendIntervalViolationError (see [SWS_CM_10432]) shall be returned via the
ara::core::Future of the operator(). For Fire&Forget methods, the call shall
be discarded, but no further error is reported back to the application, i.e., the applica-
tion has to expect that F&F method calls are not executed in case of an Minimum Send
Interval violation without further feedback by ara::com. The Minimum Send Interval
shall only be check on the client side, i.e., by the instance that actually invokes the
method call and not by the server/provider, which answers/accepts the method call. If
the configured Minimum Send Interval (ServiceInterfaceDeploymentElement.
minimumSendInterval) of a method has the value 0, the Minimum Send Interval
monitoring shall not be active for the corresponding operator().
⌋
